prompt: Route a command name to a method by matching the value inside its @Command annotation, then invoke that method reflectively. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: An annotation with a value() member turns a method into a self-describing table entry, so the dispatcher never needs a switch that has to be edited every time a command is added. getAnnotation returns null when the marker is absent, which is exactly the filter you want -- unannotated methods such as helper stay invisible. Method.invoke passes arguments as varargs and returns Object, so an int result arrives boxed as an Integer and has to be cast before it can be returned. Throwing for an unknown command keeps the failure obvious instead of silently returning 0.
hints: Loop over target.getClass().getDeclaredMethods() and ask each one for method.getAnnotation(Command.class); skip it when that is null.
Compare marker.value() with the requested command using equals, not ==.
method.invoke(target, a, b) returns Object. Cast it to Integer to return an int, and wrap the call in a try/catch for the checked reflective exceptions.
